done: idek why i bothered trying to watch this in japanese, clearly way above my level but opensubtitles had soft jp subs so i thought why not give it a shot... well the western japanese/hiroshima-ben nearly killed me >< so many things i had to look up that weren't in any of my yomitan dictionaries... luckily the visuals made it pretty clear what was going on even if i couldn't figure out what was being said. as for the movie, i’ve somehow never watched a single yakuza movie despite being obsessed with the yakuza video game franchise for more than like. four years. so when i stumbled upon [this film recommendation list](https://thegenrejunkie.com/the-20-best-yakuza-films/) of the 20 best yakuza movies which had this series of five movies at the top i was like okay, not a film girlie but why not give the best one a shot… idk how to put this but there’s something about the way violence is depicted in this movie that i find much more watchable than most of the live-action violence i’ve seen. i’m actually very bad with live-action gore, horror, violence, etc despite reading/playing lots of violent manga, books, and games but watching this movie, beyond one or two scenes it didn’t bother me too much. maybe special effects now are more realistic than the 70s, but i found that the clearly not-real violence and deaths in this movie didn’t take away from their gravitas. throughout watching the movie, i wasn’t actually sure whether i was enjoying it or not (probably because my brain was spending too much power trying to decipher the language lol) but by the last office scene between hirono, makihara, and yamamori, the bedroom scene between hirono and sakai, and especially the final funeral scene i definitely found myself wanting to continue watching hirono’s story in the next movie.
